newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - Shandong Xinhua debut seen strong.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Shandong Xinhua debut seen strong.

text.p: Shandong Xinhua Pharmaceutical Co Ltd shares are poised for a strong trading debut on Tuesday, bucking the trend of weak H-share market debuts in 1996 and paving the way for similar new listings in 1997, analysts said.

A strong trading debut is expected for the medicine maker due to its high grey market price and a warm response to its initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong, compared with five other H-shares -- mainland Chinese companies with Hong Kong listings -- which had their debuts in 1996, they said.
Analysts said the grey market price of shares of Shandong Xinhua was about HK$2.40 each versus their offer price of HK$1.82.

A relatively low price-to-earnings (P.E.) mutliple of 5.8 times on the weighted average basis of the issue, compared with its counterpart China Pharmaceutical Enterprise and Investment Corp Ltd, had also fueled upside expectations.
China Pharmaceutical, a vitamin C maker, is trading at a P.E. of about 35 times.
"Shandong Xinhua is hot because of stronger demand for H-shares and red-chips ahead of Hong Kong's 1997 handover to China," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
Shandong Xinhua, the last H-share to be listed in Hong Kong in 1996, engages in the development, manufacture and sales of bulk pharmaceutical, preparation and chemical products.

It offered 140 million H-shares at HK$1.82 per share with an over-allotment option for up to another 10 million H-shares at the same price. Its IPO public subscription portion was 94 times subscribed.

Shandong Xinhua said proceeds would be used to upgrade production technology in its existing factory and for building new assembly lines for new products. The balance will be used for repaying bank loans and as working capital.

"It (a strong performance) will aid a bit the (H-shares) market sentiment towards their IPOs, at least giving hints on how investors like the sector at this stage," said Kinson Au, senior analysts at PW Asia Brokerage.

Analysts said Chinese enterprises had disappointed investors due to a poor earnings outlook after being hit by China's austerity measures. Investors were mostly staying away from the sector after they burnt their fingers, analysts said.

In 1996, five Chinese companies' H-shares were listed in Hong Kong, including Jingwei Textile Machinery Co Ltd, Nanjing Panda Electronics Co Ltd, Guangshen Railway Co Ltd, Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd, and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd.
Apart from Jingwei Textile and Guangshen Railway, which came through their debuts seven percent up from their issue prices, others dived on their first day of trading.

"Even though the market is still mixed on the sector, the expected strong debut performance (of Shandong Xinhua) will psychologically reignite investors' interest in H-shares," one research manager said.
"It is paving the way for other upcoming H-shares," he said.
The recent rally in China's own stock markets also convinced investors of a pick-up in Hong Kong's H-shares, analysts said.

Analysts generally expect more H-shares to seek a Hong Kong listing in 1997, tapping local market strength and exploiting the existing strong demand for China-related stocks ahead of the territory's return to China on July 1, 1997.
Shenzhen Freeway Development Co Ltd's H-shares and China Eastern Airline are expected to seek listings in early 1997.
"Investors are favouring China concept stocks...especially those having direct exposure to the China market", Alex Tang, research director from Yamaichi International, said.
Analysts said they expected Chinese companies' earnings to turn around in the fiscal years ending during 1997 and 1998, after being hard hit by austerity measures in recent years.
